analysis:
The only change in this PR is a single documentation row added at docs/reference/configuration.md line 413. It documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. No executable code or security control changes in the supplied evidence. I read the surrounding units (head lines 1-519) for context.

Security-relevant claims in the new row:
- It is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. That is a provider-local tuning env var and not a secret-bearing or auth-related one.
- It says the warmup runs a 128-token shader-cache probe twice, runs the shape cells only on a cold cache, and is bounded to 20 seconds per engine.
- It says the warmup trains no rate or counter.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle): the row does not touch the prefix cache. The warmup is described as excluded and as training no counter, so it should not alter cache state or the encrypted SSD tier. The warmup input content is not shown. If warmup used real consumer prompts, A-001 exposure would be a concern, but the 128-token probe is described as synthetic.
- T-010 and T-029 (availability): the 20-second per-engine cap bounds the startup delay.

Unverified contract: I could not see ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (shapeWarmupMode) or the architecture/inference.md#model-startup-calibration anchor. I cannot confirm that the code matches the documented bound, that the warmup is truly synthetic, or that warmup does not touch the prefix cache. Those belong to the implementation PR, not to this documentation-only diff.

No findings qualify. needs_deeper_review=false because the diff is documentation only.
